events.text: The market is shorter of people than it should be, and nobody mentions it. On the road out of town you pass the gate of {ih_house}. It is open. The plaque is still up. A {ih_colour} banner hangs over it that was not there at the new moon, and the two young men on the steps have the uneasy manners of people told to be polite.

choices.text: Keep walking

effects.log: You keep walking. One of them bows. You wish he had not.

choices.text: Ask them who their master is now

effects.log: They look at each other. "The same," says one, and the other looks at the banner. You have your answer.

choices.text: Leave a little silver with their old gatekeeper

effects.log: He takes it without looking at you. It will buy rice for someone who cannot ask.

events.text: A cart comes through at dusk with the tablets of {ih_house} tied down under a tarpaulin, and a very old woman sitting on them with a cleaver in her lap. The rest of the house is still up the valley, she says, learning new songs for {ih_by}. She is taking the ancestors somewhere they will not have to hear it.

choices.text: Walk beside the cart to the county line

effects.log: She does not thank you. At the county line she looks at your hands and says you may tell people she was not alone.

choices.text: Tell her which roads are watched

effects.log: She has you say it twice and then repeats it perfectly. The cart turns off before the bridge.

choices.text: Stand aside

effects.log: You stand aside. The cart goes past, and its axle needs oil.

events.text: In {ih_place} they no longer say that {ih_house} fell. They say it has been asked to help. Its elders still sit in the same chairs, and every tenth day an accountant from {ih_by} comes and sits in a chair beside them. Its disciples still practise at dawn, though the forms have begun to end differently.

choices.text: Watch the dawn practice from the wall

effects.log: You watch long enough to see what has been changed. It is well taught, which is the worst of it.

choices.text: Buy the accountant a drink

effects.log: He is pleasant and tired and says nothing at all, and he pays for the second round. You like him, which you had not planned on.

choices.text: Go home

effects.log: You go home by the other road.

events.text: A boy from {ih_house} is washing dishes at the inn. His hands still have the calluses. When you look at them he puts them under the water. He says he left before the {ih_colour} banners came. The cook says he left the night they did, over a wall, with a broken wrist, and that nobody needs to hear about it.

choices.text: Leave him to the dishes

effects.log: You leave him to the dishes. Some mornings a person only wants to be a person who washes dishes.

choices.text: Show him one way to bind that wrist properly

effects.log: He lets you. Neither of you mentions why you know how. He holds the next bowl a little better.

choices.text: Ask what happened to his master

effects.log: He thinks about it for some time, and says that his master is doing very well, and takes the next dish.

events.text: The seniors read the name of {ih_house} from the roll of friends at morning assembly, and then it does not read anything for a moment. By noon the seniors have decided that the road to {ih_place} is closed to juniors. By evening the juniors know exactly how to get there.

choices.text: Keep to the yard

effects.log: You keep to the yard. Two of the juniors do not, and one comes back.

choices.text: Go to the senior who closed the road and ask why

effects.log: They shut the door first. "Because we are next," they say, "and I would like to have someone left." It is not the answer you were expecting.

events.text: They come at the second watch, forty or so, with the sick on doors. {Ih_house} was theirs until {ih_by} asked for its gate and its accounts. Their last elder kneels in your yard and asks for one winter under your roof. Your steward has already counted the rice, and is standing where you can see his face.

choices.text: Open the halls: one winter, and as long as it takes after

effects.log: The rice goes down quickly. So does the talk in the teahouses about how safe you are. Nobody who has slept on a door forgets where they slept next.

choices.text: Rice at the gate, and no further

effects.log: They eat at the gate and go on in the morning. The elder bows exactly as far as is correct.

choices.text: Send word to {ih_by} that you have them

effects.log: They are gone before the rice is cooked. You will be told it was the only sensible thing, by everyone who would like to stay on your good side.

events.text: A letter comes up the road tied to the wrist of a child, because nobody else from {ih_house} could get through. It is one line in a firm hand. It asks if your gate is open, and gives no reason to think anyone would be grateful. The child has been told to wait for an answer, and has started on your persimmons.

choices.text: Send your people out to bring them in

effects.log: Your people go by the back roads and bring in sixty, and the tablets, and a goat that nobody will explain. There is less room in the halls now, and more noise.

choices.text: Write back that you cannot, and feed the child

effects.log: You write it twice. The child reads it, which you had not expected, and keeps the persimmons.

choices.text: Keep the child, and send no answer

effects.log: Nobody ever comes for the answer. The child stays and learns to sweep. It is, you tell yourself, a kind of answer.

events.text: An envoy of {ih_by} takes your tea and mentions, between other things, that the leadership of {ih_house} ran off with some records, and might be on the {ih_place} road. He says it mildly. He has seen the cart tracks at your back gate. So have you, this morning, and you have not yet asked your steward about them.

choices.text: Tell him you take in whom you please

effects.log: He finishes his tea. He says that is good to know, in the voice of a man writing it down later. In the back hall forty people breathe out.

choices.text: Send him to the back hall yourself

effects.log: He thanks you in front of your people. You have not been thanked like that before, and you will not forget how quiet the yard is afterwards.

choices.text: Have the steward move them on before nightfall

effects.log: They are on the road by dusk with a sack of your rice. Nobody has lied to anyone. You sleep badly anyway.

events.text: A rider in {ih_colour} leaves a scroll at your gate. It is very civil. {Ih_house} has already accepted the friendship of {ih_by}, and it is hoped you will find it convenient to do likewise: a list of your people, a share of your silver, and a man at your table every tenth day. The rider will return in a month.

choices.text: Pay for a season of being overlooked

effects.log: The silver goes down the road in plain boxes. Your people are told it is for a bridge. The rider does not come back this year.

choices.text: Send the scroll back with the seal unbroken

effects.log: You send it back. Your senior disciples start sleeping in their boots, and you notice they seem happier for it.

choices.text: Answer slowly, with many questions

effects.log: You ask about the wording. Then about the seal. Then whether the bridge toll counts. It takes them until the snow to notice.

events.text: {npc} of {ih_by} does not bother with a scroll. {He} sits down in your hall in muddy boots, tells you what {ih_house} agreed to, and tells you what became of the one elder there who did not. {He} is about thirty, and there is nothing in {his} face at all. {He} asks where you would like the banner hung.

choices.text: Show {him} where

ok.log: {He} leaves by the gate on {his} own legs, which is more than {he} had planned to offer you. It will be told at length, and not by {him}.

fail.log: {He} is better than the boots. {He} leaves without the answer {he} came for, but you do the rest of the talking sitting down.

choices.text: Pay {him} to hang it nowhere

effects.log: {He} counts it. {He} says this will do for now, and that now does not last. Your disciples do not look at you for a while.

events.text: Your own elders want it talked through, so it is talked through until the lamps go out. {Ih_house} bowed and lost its gate anyway. {Ih_house} had four hundred people and you know how many you have. The youngest of them says something unforgivable about {ih_by}, and then, to your surprise, the eldest agrees.

choices.text: Say that you will not bow, and let them hear it

effects.log: It is very quiet, then very loud. There will be no more talk of it, and a great deal of sharpening.

choices.text: Say that you will pay this once, and take the shame on yourself

effects.log: The elders look relieved, which is hard to forgive. The boxes go out by night. You sign for them under your own name.

choices.text: Say nothing tonight, and send a very polite letter

effects.log: The letter takes four drafts. It says nothing whatever, beautifully, and it buys the winter.

events.text: {npc} has not eaten since the carter came. {He} was raised in {ih_house}, you knew that, the way you know the name of someone's old dog. Now {he} tells you the rest: a sister in the kitchens, two old teachers, a nephew who writes. Nobody has written. {He} does not ask you for anything. {He} just keeps not eating at you.

choices.text: Send silver and a good man up the road to find them

effects.log: The man comes back in forty days with the nephew and a list of who cannot leave. {npc} reads it standing up. Then {he} eats.

choices.text: Go with {him} yourself

effects.log: It takes a month and you see more of {ih_place} than you wished. You find the sister, who will not leave the others, but who has now been found.

choices.text: Tell {him} there is nothing to be done yet

effects.log: It is true. {He} nods, and it is a long time before {he} talks to you about anything but the weather.

events.text: A note from {ih_house} reaches {npc}, in the hand of the one who taught {him} to hold a brush. It says that everyone is well, that the new teachers are excellent, and that {he} should come home and see the place. {npc} puts it on the table in front of you. "My old teacher has never once in a long life used the word excellent," {he} says.

choices.text: Tell {him} not to go, and say why

effects.log: {He} does not go, and is angry for a month, and is still here at the end of it.

choices.text: Pay a pedlar to carry a question only the writer could answer

effects.log: The answer comes back in the same hand, and it is the wrong answer on purpose. So the old teacher is still in there. {npc} keeps that one in {his} sleeve.

choices.text: Let {him} make up {his} own mind

effects.log: {He} goes. {He} comes back in a season, thinner, and does not talk about it. You are glad, and you do not say so.

events.text: Over the evening rice {npc} says it as if it were news about the price of salt: {Ih_house} took the {ih_colour} banner this spring, and {his} first master stood at the gate to welcome it. Then {he} reaches for the pickles. It takes you a moment to see that {his} hand is not quite steady.

choices.text: Ask about the master

effects.log: It takes until the lamp burns low. You had never heard any of it, and you are the only one who ever will.

choices.text: Pass the pickles, and talk of the salt

effects.log: You talk of salt. {He} looks grateful, and goes to bed early.

choices.text: Quietly pay what {ih_house} owed the county, so the elders have one less rope

effects.log: It will not change the banner. {npc} finds out in a year or so, from someone else, and never mentions it, and starts leaving the good cup out for you.

events.text: Your hall is told off to accept the surrender of {ih_house}. It is a modest place. The elders have their robes pressed. Their eldest offers you the gate keys on a tray with both hands, and his hands shake, and he looks at the wall while they shake. Your seniors wait to see how you will take the keys.

choices.text: Take them with both hands, and bow

effects.log: You bow. Your seniors note it, and so does the old man, and only one of them will ever thank you. The house keeps its kitchens and its name.

choices.text: Let them hold the tray a little longer

effects.log: You let them hold it. Nobody tells you to do this. Later that year you notice nobody has to.

choices.text: Have the tablets taken down and burned

effects.log: It is done by evening. Nobody in that valley will ever say the name again, not in front of anyone. The Hall commends you.

events.text: You are given the rolls of {ih_house} to check. It is dull work, names and ages, who has which forms. You find two children marked to be taken to the mountains for training, and you find the clerk has written in the margin, very small, in a hand that hopes not to be read: their mother is the cook.

choices.text: Lose that page

effects.log: Pages get lost. You will not be asked, and if you are asked, you lost it.

choices.text: Pass it on as written

effects.log: The rolls go up the mountain. So do the children, in the second cart. The margin was not your business, and you go on telling yourself so.

choices.text: Have the clerk brought in, and ask why he wrote it

effects.log: He weeps. You did not want that either. You send him back to his desk, and he never writes in a margin again.

events.text: A young disciple of {ih_house} has gone over the wall, and you are the one on the road when they bring in his tracks. He has a day on you and a bad ankle. You could have him by nightfall. It would be noticed and rewarded. It would also be noticed if you came back with nothing, and the road forks twice.

choices.text: Take the wrong fork, both times

effects.log: You come back at dusk with nothing and a good story about the fog. Someone looks at you for slightly too long.

choices.text: Bring him back alive

effects.log: He does not struggle much. You put him on your own horse for the last mile. He does not thank you, and he is right.

choices.text: Bring back the ankle boot and leave the rest of it

effects.log: You find him. You come back with his boot, and you say what you are expected to say, and nobody needs to know he is alive.

events.text: As one who sits high under {ih_by}, you are sent the plan for {ih_place} to approve: which small houses keep their gates, which are folded in, which are not to be spoken of. {Ih_house} has a mark beside it you know the meaning of. It is one stroke of your brush, either way. The runner has been told to wait.

choices.text: Strike the mark out: let them keep the gate

effects.log: You strike it out. It will not make you loved. It will be argued about for a season, and then {ih_house} will have outlived the argument.

choices.text: Sign it as it stands

effects.log: You sign it, and the runner bows. It takes less time than the tea.

choices.text: Add a mark of your own: finish it

effects.log: A clean stroke. There will be no one to have the argument. You put down the brush and find you are not thinking of anything.

events.text: A sack of millet at your door has a strip of cloth in it, and on the cloth a list: the hours of the guard at {ih_house}, the number of men from {ih_by}, and the night the moon is down. There are thirty of the old disciples ready to open the postern, it says. They have no one who can stand against the overseer, {npc}.

choices.text: Be there the night the moon is down

ok.log: The overseer goes down on the steps. Thirty people you have never met pull the {ih_colour} banner off the gate and do not stop to thank you. {Ih_house} is its own again, for as long as it can hold.

fail.log: The overseer is better than the list said. You get out by the postern with a hole in you, and you hope some of the thirty did too.

choices.text: Burn the cloth

effects.log: You burn it. On the night the moon is down you stay in, and you do not sleep, and in the morning nobody mentions anything.

events.text: The old gatekeeper of {ih_house} comes to you in a fish porter's hat. The overseer from {ih_by}, {npc}, drinks at the ferry inn every fifth day, with two men, and the ferry is out of sight of everything. There are people in that house who would come back to themselves, says the old voice, if somebody only showed them it could be done.

choices.text: Go down to the ferry on the fifth day

ok.log: It is over before the wine is poured. By morning the banner on {ih_house} has been taken down by someone, and nobody at all saw who. It is a very small victory, and the whole county is walking differently.

fail.log: Two men was a lie, or an old count. You swim. The fish porter's hat is the last thing you see of the gatekeeper.

choices.text: Give the old one money for the road, and say to go

effects.log: The money goes into the hat. The gatekeeper is too old to be proud, and too old to go far.

events.text: The war is over, and {ih_house} has its gate again, and a good deal less of everything else. Their new head walks up your road on foot with a chest two men could carry. It holds the deed to a tea hill and what is left of their silver. "It is not payment," the head says. "We would like it known that we can still count."

choices.text: Take it, and set them a place at your table every New Year

effects.log: You take it, and you are careful how. {Ih_house} sends you a hill's worth of tea every spring from then on, and news you would not otherwise hear.

choices.text: Give it back, and ask for their sword forms for your library

effects.log: They look relieved, and then ashamed of it. The forms are copied by hand, in a hand you recognise from a letter.

events.text: When the {ih_colour} banners went back, {ih_house} came home, and the first thing they did was send someone to you. You have not met this one: {he} stands straighter than a person with that limp should, and looks at your gate as if counting it. {He} has brought no gift. {He} says that three of theirs would like to learn under you, and stay, and that they eat very little.

choices.text: Take the three in

effects.log: They eat a great deal, and work like oxen, and they tell no one where they came from unless someone says something about you.

choices.text: Send them home with your thanks

effects.log: They go home. A year later there is a shrine with a very bad likeness of you in it, and you decide not to visit.

events.text: A cart of pickled mustard comes to your gate with no letter. Under the mustard is a list of every debt {ih_by} ever claimed in {ih_place}, written out from memory by someone who sat beside its accountant for years. {Ih_house} is back behind its own gate. It would seem they have a sense of humour after all, and a long memory.

choices.text: Eat the mustard, and read the list closely

effects.log: The mustard is excellent. The list is better. You know three things now about three people that they would pay to have you forget.

choices.text: Burn the list and send back a jar of your own

effects.log: You send back a jar. Yours is worse. They write to say so, which is, you understand, friendship.

events.text: {Ih_house} came home after the war with fewer people than it left with. You know why some of them are missing, and so do they. {npc} has walked to your gate alone. {He} is not armed in any way you can see. {He} says the names you handed over, one at a time, without hurrying, and then {he} waits for you.

choices.text: Answer with your hands

ok.log: {He} stays down. Nobody from {ih_house} comes to fetch {him}; they knew what they were sending. There will be others, or there will not. You say the names over to yourself, later, to see if you still can.

fail.log: {He} has practised for this for years. You will have that limp for a while. {He} turns at your gate, and comes back next spring, and the one after, until {he} is done with you.

choices.text: Hear the names through, and bow

effects.log: You bow. It does not help, and {he} never said it would. But {he} goes home, and you stop hearing about {ih_house} at all.

choices.text: Pay the blood price, in front of everyone

effects.log: {He} counts it in front of everyone, and leaves it on the ground, and walks home. Your disciples have to pick it up.

events.text: People have stopped selling you things in {ih_place}. It takes you a while to notice. It is {ih_house}, back behind its gate, smaller, and in no hurry. They have not said a word against you. They have only told, at every well in three counties, exactly what happened on the night you gave them up to {ih_by}.

choices.text: Send them the worth of what was lost

effects.log: It comes back with one coin taken out of it. Nobody can tell you what that means, and everybody seems to know.

choices.text: Go in person and say it was you

effects.log: You say it at their gate. It is quiet, and it is not forgiven, and on your way out of the county a woman sells you an onion.

choices.text: Outlast them

effects.log: You outlast them, you suppose. It is the same as being disliked for a long time by people who remember why.

events.text: The {ih_colour} banner over {ih_house} comes down without any ceremony, on a wet morning, because the people it belonged to have gone home. An old man takes it off the gate and folds it. He has folded it neatly. The house is smaller, and it has a new way of not meeting your eye, but on the third day the smoke goes up from its kitchens.

choices.text: Go past and say good morning

effects.log: You say good morning. The old man looks at you for a while, and says good morning.

choices.text: Send over a sack of rice, no name on it

effects.log: There is no thanks, as you meant it. The next week they send over a jar with no name on it.

events.text: People from {ih_house} have come back through {ih_place} in ones and twos, and the old plaque is up over the gate again, a little crooked. They have kept some of what they were taught. You saw a boy in their yard finish a form the way {ih_by} finishes it, and an elder cuff him, and then, when he thought nobody saw, try it himself.

choices.text: Say nothing about what you saw

effects.log: You say nothing. Everyone here has got very good at that.

choices.text: Tell the elder it was a good cuff

effects.log: He looks at you, then laughs, for what seems to be the first time in some years.

events.text: {Ih_house} has come back, and it has not taken the banner down. The war is over, {ih_by} has gone home, and still the {ih_colour} cloth hangs over the gate by the choice of those who stayed. "We have found the teaching sound," their new head says, pleasantly, to anyone who asks. It is hard to say who asked for it first.

choices.text: Keep your distance

effects.log: You keep your distance. So does most of {ih_place}. Oddly, they seem to have more visitors than they did.

choices.text: Call on them, and take a good look

effects.log: You take a good look. The rice is good, and the children are fed, and nobody will sit with their back to a door. You leave before dark.

events.text: The new head of {ih_house} was its kitchen girl when the banners came. Everyone over her head went up the mountain or into the river. She held the place together for years with lies and bookkeeping, and now she sits in the high seat in the same apron, and the elders who have come home from the mountain find they are to ask her first.

choices.text: Pay your respects, apron and all

effects.log: She looks you over the way she looks at a fish. "You will do," she says, and sends you off with something to eat.

choices.text: Ask how she managed it

effects.log: She tells you some of it. You come away thinking the great sects have been choosing leaders the wrong way.

events.text: Before, nobody crossed the road for {ih_house}. Now they come home harder than they left: fewer, quieter, and with what they took from the overseers as well as what they learned from them. A bandit tried the toll on their road last month. He is still on their road, in several places, as a kind of signpost.

choices.text: Mention to them that the county has laws

effects.log: Their head agrees, warmly. That is the end of the conversation, and you feel you have got away with something.

choices.text: Ask if they take visiting swords

effects.log: They do. You go home with a bruise and a very different idea of who was the small house.

events.text: The war is over and the road to {ih_house} is open again, and you go up it because someone ought to. Nobody has come back. The plaque is on the ground and the yard is high with weeds. In the kitchen someone has laid out one bowl for each of them, in rows, on the good table, and then, it seems, walked away.

choices.text: Stand the plaque up against the wall

effects.log: You stand it against the wall. It is not much. It is more than anyone else did.

choices.text: Count the bowls

effects.log: You count them. You will not be able to say why, but when anyone asks, you can tell them how many there were.

choices.text: Go back down

effects.log: You go back down. The weeds are full of crickets, and the path is very pretty at this time of year.

events.text: In {ih_place} a storyteller is doing the fall of {ih_house}, and he has got it wrong: there was no duel on the bridge, and no last elder holding the pass. There was an ordinary morning and a list. Nobody corrects him. A woman at the back, who might have been from there, puts down her coin when he is done, and it is the only coin all night.

choices.text: Put a coin down beside hers

effects.log: She looks at it, and at you. You both go out by different doors.

choices.text: Ask her what it really was

effects.log: She looks at you for a long moment. "A house," she says. "Why does everyone want it to be more?"
